title: What is the side of this square, and the roots of sixty four?
description: The video finds the side of a square from its area of sixty four square centimetres, and gives both square roots of sixty four. Keeko doubts the roots after saying sixty four has only one, forgetting that a negative number squared is also positive.
teaching_notes: One idea: a square root of a number is a number that gives it when multiplied by itself, and a positive number has two of them, one positive and one negative. Watch for students who give only the positive root, or who say the side can be negative.

source: A square has area 64 square cm. Find its side, and give both square roots of 64.
video_script.why: The child connects the side of a square to the square root of its area, and sees that a number has a positive and a negative square root while a side is a length.
video_script.substitution: Find the number that multiplies itself to give the area, then check the negative of it too.
video_script.anchor: a square of area sixty four square centimetres with its side marked by a question mark
video_script.wrong_answer: only one square root, which is eight
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says 64 has only one square root, 8. But (−8) × (−8) = 64 too, so 64 has two square roots, 8 and −8; the side of the square is the positive one.
video_script.payoff_line: The side is eight centimetres, and the square roots of sixty four are eight and minus eight

final_answer.value: The side is 8 cm; the square roots of 64 are 8 and −8
final_answer.spoken: the side is eight centimetres, and the square roots of sixty four are eight and minus eight

hold_back: The side is 8 cm; the square roots of 64 are 8 and −8
never_show: the square root of 441 of the exercise video
maths_rules: area of a square = side × side, so s × s = 64
(−8) × (−8) = 64, because a negative times a negative is positive, so the square roots of 64 are 8 and −8
a side is a length, so it is the positive root, 8 cm
ground: a side of 3 cm gives an area of 9 square cm, and 3 × 3 = 9
video_script.design: One idea: two numbers multiply themselves to give sixty four, but a side takes the positive one. Wrong idea: only one root. The square stays in the anchor band and the roots fill in on the working board.
